recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. The current build-scope conformance page is correct for FHIR-12227 after the later approved CapabilityStatement wording decisions, and no separate seed-specific edit is needed.
issue_request: FHIR-12227 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core request to add text explaining that any assertion of FHIR conformance without a ConformanceStatement instance has limited utility and that capabilities not describable by a ConformanceStatement cannot be considered FHIR conformant.
initial_application: The request was applied in commit 3d7763fc7d0a1a1921562cf73de46c53197d669e on 2016-11-04, matching the Jira svn @10126 comment and adding the requested paragraph to source/conformance-rules.html. Later terminology evolved from ConformanceStatement to CapabilityStatement.
additional_context: Later published issues intentionally refined the same paragraph: FHIR-16084 replaced the second sentence with the affirmative rule that systems can only claim FHIR conformance for functionality described in an applicable CapabilityStatement, FHIR-18040 linked the CapabilityStatement reference, FHIR-18041 struck the awkward original 'limited utility' sentence, and FHIR-19575 added the current REST/non-server clarification and testability statement. The related later issues already have reconcile records on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/conformance-rules.html currently states that systems can only claim FHIR conformance for functionality described in the applicable CapabilityStatement, RESTful servers must provide one on request, and formal conformance assertions without one have little meaning because they cannot be tested or verified.
